title: The Last Summer on Maple Street
author: Daniel Reyes
pages:
June 2nd.

Mom says the news is making it sound worse than it is. Dad stopped going to work on Monday. The school sent a letter home saying classes are cancelled "until further notice."

I'm writing this down because Mr. Hale always said history is just people who bothered to write things down.

June 5th.

The Novera trucks came through again this morning. White vans, no windows in the back. They were handing out little blue bottles at the gas station. "Better Medicine, Better Health."

Dad wouldn't take one. He said nobody gives anything away for free.

June 9th.

The Hendersons' lights stayed on all night. Nobody answered when we knocked. Dad told me to stay inside and keep the curtains shut.

At night you can hear them walking. Slow. Like they forgot how.

June 14th.

The power went out for good today. Dad says light is the worst thing you can have now — they come for it.

We boarded up the windows with the planks from the old fence. I'm writing this by the last of the daylight.

June 20th.

We're leaving tomorrow for the hospital. Somebody on the radio said the hospitals still have power.

If you found this book: the spare key is under the blue flower pot. There's canned beans in the basement. Take them.

Good luck.

— Danny
